intent.raw_query: Mexico City food and culture, $900 solo, 5 days, any month 2026

experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most iconic gourmet markets, sampling local delicacies like tlayudas, exotic cheeses, fresh ceviche, and traditional Mexican street food. Interact with local vendors and discover ingredients central to Mexican cuisine.

experiences.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología Visit
experiences.description: Discover one of the world's greatest anthropology museums, housing extraordinary pre-Columbian artifacts including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. Gain deep insight into Mexico's rich indigenous cultures, history, and civilizations spanning thousands of years.

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood Walking Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the bohemian cobblestone streets of Coyoacán, visiting the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul), colorful local markets, and the historic central plaza. Sample local street food like tostadas and churros from neighborhood vendors.

experiences.name: Tacos and Mezcal Evening in Roma Norte
experiences.description: Experience Mexico City's vibrant culinary nightlife in the trendy Roma Norte neighborhood. Visit acclaimed taco stands like El Turix for cochinita pibil and pair your meal with artisanal mezcal at a local cantina, immersing yourself in authentic local dining culture.

experiences.name: Teotihuacán Pyramids Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a short bus ride to the awe-inspiring ancient city of Teotihuacán and climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon. Explore the Avenue of the Dead, visit local artisan stalls, and enjoy a traditional Mexican lunch at a nearby restaurant.
experiences.location: Teotihuacán, State of Mexico (50 km northeast of Mexico City)

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle into Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — arrival is in the evening. Use travel time to review your Mexico City plan.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City airport at 22:30. Take the Metro Line 5 from Terminal Aérea station (very budget-friendly at ~$0.25 USD) or a pre-booked authorized airport taxi to your hotel. Check in, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack near the hotel.

meals.dinner: Late-night taco stand or 24-hour OXXO convenience store near the hotel for a quick, cheap bite (tacos de canasta ~$0.50–$1 each)

day_by_day.notes: Only use official airport taxi booths (TAPO or authorized counters) to avoid scams. The Metro is the cheapest option at ~5 MXN. Have some pesos ready upon arrival. Day 1 is purely an arrival day — no sightseeing scheduled.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Mexico City adventure at the historic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución) — one of the largest city squares in the world and completely free to visit. Explore the impressive Metropolitan Cathedral (free entry) and admire the exterior of the National Palace, which houses Diego Rivera's famous murals (free entry with ID).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Templo Mayor archaeological site (~$4 USD entry), the ancient Aztec temple ruins in the heart of the city. Afterward, stroll through the charming streets of Centro Histórico, browsing local artisan markets like Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela for cultural souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Alameda Central park area as the sun sets. Enjoy the street performers and local atmosphere. Walk along Avenida Madero, a pedestrian street full of energy, historic buildings, and free street art.

meals.breakfast: Café de chinos or a local fondita near the hotel — chilaquiles or tamales with atole (~$2–$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan or a nearby mercado comedor — comida corrida (set lunch menu with soup, main, and drink) for ~$3–$5 USD
meals.dinner: Taquería El Huequito in Centro Histórico — famous for tacos al pastor, ~$1–$1.50 per taco. Budget ~$4–$6 USD total

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Centro Histórico is best explored on foot. Keep belongings secure in crowded areas. The Metro is your best friend for getting around cheaply.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán, one of Mexico City's most charming and culturally rich neighborhoods. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets online in advance (~$4–$5 USD). Explore the cobblestone streets and colorful colonial architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Mercado de Coyoacán for lunch and browsing. Afterward, visit the free Viveros de Coyoacán park — a beautiful green space popular with locals. Walk to the Plaza Hidalgo and Jardín Centenario to soak in the neighborhood's bohemian vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Metro to Colonia Roma Norte, a hip and artsy neighborhood. Walk along Álvaro Obregón avenue, lined with trees, sculptures, and street art. Browse the area's vibrant street food scene.

meals.breakfast: Local panadería (bakery) near the hotel — pan dulce and café de olla for ~$1–$2 USD
meals.lunch: Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — try tostadas de tinga or enchiladas for ~$2–$4 USD
meals.dinner: Street tacos in Colonia Roma — look for busy stands with long lines (a sign of quality). Budget ~$4–$6 USD for 4–5 tacos

day_by_day.notes: Coyoacán is very walkable once you arrive. Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly. The Metro ride from Centro to Coyoacán takes about 30–40 minutes and costs just a few pesos.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Metro + bus or pesero (local minibus) to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Aztec city of pyramids (~1 hour from the city, ~$3–$4 USD round trip by bus from Terminal Central del Norte). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon — entry is ~$5 USD. Arrive early to beat the crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Avenue of the Dead and the Temple of Quetzalcóatl at Teotihuacán. Spend a full afternoon immersed in this UNESCO World Heritage Site. Return to Mexico City by late afternoon via the same bus route.
day_by_day.evening: Recover with a relaxed evening in the Tepito or Garibaldi Plaza area. Garibaldi is famous for its Mariachi bands that play freely in the square — a truly authentic Mexican cultural experience at no cost.

meals.breakfast: Grab tamales and atole from a street vendor near the Metro station before departure (~$1.50–$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Food stalls just outside the Teotihuacán site entrance — quesadillas, tlayudas, and fresh fruit for ~$3–$5 USD
meals.dinner: Mercado Medellín or a local fondita back in the city — pozole or mole with rice and beans ~$4–$6 USD

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water for Teotihuacán — it is very exposed and can be hot. Wear sturdy shoes for climbing the pyramids. Buses to Teotihuacán depart regularly from Terminal Central del Norte (Metro Autobuses del Norte, Line 5).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the world and completely free to enter. Stroll through the park, visit Chapultepec Lake, and enjoy the local atmosphere with families and joggers. The Castillo de Chapultepec (National History Museum) offers stunning city views and rich history for ~$3 USD entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to the Museo Nacional de Antropología — one of the world's greatest museums and a must-see for culture lovers (~$4 USD entry). Spend 2–3 hours exploring Aztec, Maya, and other pre-Hispanic civilizations' artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Mercado de la Merced or Mercado Jamaica for a final authentic local market experience. Pick up local spices, chocolates, or crafts as affordable souvenirs. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a classic Mexico City restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Café El Popular in Centro or a local torta stand — torta de jamón or huevos rancheros ~$2–$3 USD
meals.lunch: Café/restaurant inside or near Chapultepec — comida corrida for ~$4–$5 USD
meals.dinner: El Cardenal restaurant (budget-friendly traditional Mexican cuisine) or a local fondita in Centro Histórico — mole, chiles en nogada, or pozole ~$6–$8 USD for a satisfying farewell meal

day_by_day.notes: Sunday entry to the Museo Nacional de Antropología is free for Mexican citizens but still ~$4 USD for international visitors. Chapultepec is most lively on weekends. Pack light for the day as you may want to pick up last-minute souvenirs at the markets.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late night arrival. Check into Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives at 22:30. Rest and prepare for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take an authorized airport taxi or pre-booked transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack at the airport or a 24-hour convenience store near the hotel (OXXO is widely available). Alternatively, order room service if available at the resort.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at 22:30. No activities are scheduled for Day 1. Ensure your hotel transfer is pre-arranged. Keep some Mexican pesos (MXN) handy for tips and small purchases. Exchange currency at the airport or use an ATM upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a visit to the Historic Center (Centro Histórico). Explore the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Walk through the Metropolitan Cathedral and admire its stunning baroque architecture. Visit the nearby Templo Mayor archaeological site to discover the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio de Bellas Artes, Mexico City's premier cultural center, to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and explore rotating art exhibitions. Stroll along Avenida Madero, a pedestrian street lined with historic buildings and street performers. Stop by the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's famous murals depicting Mexican history.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively neighborhood of Garibaldi Plaza, where Mariachi bands perform nightly. Soak in the vibrant local atmosphere and enjoy an authentic Mexican evening. Wander through the neighborhood and find a cozy local cantina for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café El Popular in Centro Histórico — a beloved local institution open 24 hours, famous for its churros with hot chocolate and traditional Mexican breakfast dishes. Budget: ~150–200 MXN per person.
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan — a mid-range indoor market near Centro Histórico offering an incredible variety of fresh local produce, cheeses, meats, and prepared foods. Try tacos de canasta or a torta. Budget: ~100–180 MXN per person.
meals.dinner: El Cardenal — a classic and beloved Mexico City restaurant in Centro Histórico known for traditional Mexican cuisine, excellent mole, and fresh-baked breads. Mid-range pricing. Budget: ~300–450 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes as Centro Histórico involves a lot of walking on cobblestones. The area is generally safe during the day and early evening but stay aware of your surroundings. Templo Mayor entry fee is approximately 85 MXN. Palacio de Bellas Artes charges a small entry fee for exhibitions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Xochimilco, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its network of ancient canals and colorful trajineras (flat-bottomed boats). Hire a trajinera and float through the canals, enjoying the lush surroundings and local vendors selling food and flowers from their own boats. This is a quintessential Mexico City cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul / The Blue House) in the charming neighborhood of Coyoacán. Explore the vibrant blue home where the iconic Mexican artist was born and lived, filled with her personal belongings, artwork, and memorabilia. Afterward, wander through the bohemian Coyoacán neighborhood, browsing its artisan markets and colorful streets.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Coyoacán's main plaza (Jardín Centenario). Enjoy street food from local vendors, watch street performers, and absorb the lively local atmosphere. This neighborhood is beloved by locals and visitors alike for its authentic Mexico City charm.

meals.breakfast: Have breakfast at the hotel or grab fresh pastries (pan dulce) and coffee from a local panadería near the resort before heading out.
meals.lunch: Enjoy lunch on your trajinera in Xochimilco — vendors on boats will approach selling fresh quesadillas, elotes (corn), and snacks. Alternatively, eat at one of the local comedores (casual eateries) near the Xochimilco embarcadero. Budget: ~150–250 MXN per person.
meals.dinner: Los Danzantes in Coyoacán — a stylish mid-range restaurant offering modern Mexican cuisine with a focus on Oaxacan flavors, mezcal cocktails, and creative dishes. Budget: ~350–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets in advance online as they sell out quickly — entry is approximately 270 MXN. Xochimilco trajinera rentals typically cost 500–700 MXN per hour for the whole boat. Coyoacán is a safe and walkable neighborhood perfect for evening exploration. March weather in Mexico City is typically warm and dry — light layers recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the world-renowned National Museum of Anthropology (Museo Nacional de Antropología) in Chapultepec Park — one of the greatest museums in the world. Spend the morning exploring its vast collection of pre-Columbian artifacts, including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. The museum alone could fill an entire day, so prioritize the Mexica (Aztec) and Maya halls.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museum, stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the world and a beloved green space for locals. Rent a rowboat on the lake, explore the park's walking paths, or visit the hilltop Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec), which offers panoramic views of the city and houses the National Museum of History.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy neighborhood of Polanco, Mexico City's upscale district known for its restaurants, boutiques, and vibrant nightlife. Stroll along Avenida Presidente Masaryk and explore the neighborhood's sophisticated atmosphere. Enjoy a mid-range dinner at one of the many excellent restaurants in the area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café near the hotel, or visit Panadería Rosetta in Roma Norte (a short trip away) — one of Mexico City's most celebrated bakeries known for its exceptional pastries and coffee. Budget: ~120–180 MXN per person.
meals.lunch: Enjoy lunch at one of the casual restaurants or food stalls near Chapultepec Park after your museum visit. Try a classic Mexican comida corrida (set lunch menu) at a local fonda for excellent value. Budget: ~120–200 MXN per person.
meals.dinner: Contramar — a legendary Mexico City seafood restaurant in the Colonia Roma neighborhood, famous for its tuna tostadas and grilled fish. Beloved by locals and food lovers worldwide. Mid-range pricing. Budget: ~350–550 MXN per person. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Anthropology entry fee is approximately 85 MXN and is free on Sundays for Mexican nationals. Chapultepec Castle entry is approximately 85 MXN. The museum is closed on Mondays. Polanco is a safe, walkable neighborhood ideal for an evening out. Uber and DiDi are reliable and affordable rideshare options throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning exploring the hip and culturally rich neighborhoods of Roma Norte and Condesa. These two adjacent neighborhoods are known for their Art Deco architecture, tree-lined boulevards, independent coffee shops, bookstores, and vibrant street art. Visit Parque México in Condesa — a beautiful oval park perfect for a morning stroll among locals walking their dogs and reading.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mercado de Medellín in Roma Sur, a fantastic local market where you can browse fresh produce, regional Mexican ingredients, and international foods. Pick up artisan souvenirs, local spices, or handmade crafts. Alternatively, explore the many independent boutiques and vintage shops along Álvaro Obregón Avenue in Roma Norte for unique gifts and mementos.
day_by_day.evening: End your trip with a farewell dinner in Roma or Condesa, two of Mexico City's best dining neighborhoods. Reflect on your incredible Mexico City experience over a final authentic Mexican meal and perhaps a mezcal or craft beer to toast the trip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café Nin or Lalo! in Colonia Roma — both are beloved local brunch spots with excellent coffee, fresh juices, and creative Mexican breakfast dishes. Expect a short wait on weekends. Budget: ~180–250 MXN per person.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Medellín — graze through the market stalls for a casual and delicious lunch sampling regional Mexican dishes, fresh fruits, and local snacks. Budget: ~100–200 MXN per person.
meals.dinner: Máximo Bistrot in Colonia Roma — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant by Chef Eduardo García, known for creative seasonal Mexican cuisine using local ingredients. A perfect farewell dinner. Mid-range to slightly upscale. Budget: ~450–650 MXN per person. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Roma and Condesa are extremely walkable neighborhoods — ideal for leisurely exploration on your last day. If you have an early departure the following day, confirm your airport transfer or taxi in advance. Consider visiting a local pharmacy for any last-minute needs as they are widely available and affordable. Leave some room in your luggage for artisan crafts, local coffee, or Mexican chocolate purchased at the markets.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late-night arrival. Rest and settle into your suite at Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — late-night arrival. Rest and settle into your suite at Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private chauffeur transfer whisks you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome amenity — chilled mezcal cocktail and seasonal fruit arranged in your suite. Familiarize yourself with the resort's luxury amenities before retiring for the night.

meals.dinner: Light late-night in-room dining from the resort's 24-hour menu — recommended: artisanal cheese board, smoked salmon blinis, and a glass of premium Mexican sparkling wine from Valle de Guadalupe

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your private airport transfer before departure. Request early check-in amenities and a pillow menu from the concierge in advance. Keep the first night light to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Begin your first full day with a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort. Afterward, embark on a private guided tour of the Historic Centro Histórico — explore the grand Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), marvel at the intricate murals inside the Palacio Nacional painted by Diego Rivera, and visit the awe-inspiring Metropolitan Cathedral. Your private guide will provide rich cultural and historical context throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its world-class museum, uncovering the Aztec empire's most sacred ceremonial center. Then stroll through the charming neighborhood of Coyoacán — wander its cobblestone streets, visit the iconic Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul), and browse the artisan market in the central plaza for high-quality crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to freshen up before heading to a premium dinner reservation at Pujol, consistently ranked among the world's best restaurants. Experience Chef Enrique Olvera's legendary Mole Madre — a mole aged over 1,000 days — paired with an expertly curated Mexican wine and mezcal tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant — eggs Benedict with huitlacoche (corn truffle), fresh tropical fruit, artisan pan dulce, and specialty Mexican coffee from Oaxacan highlands
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Cardenal in Centro Histórico — a legendary institution renowned for authentic Mexican cuisine; try the chiles en nogada (seasonal) or cochinita pibil with house-made tortillas and aguas frescas
meals.dinner: Pujol — tasting menu experience with wine and mezcal pairings (advance reservation essential; budget approx. $150–$250 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum and Pujol well in advance as both are extremely popular. Hire a private bilingual guide for Centro Histórico for a deeper cultural experience. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the historic center.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a private transfer to the ancient pre-Columbian city of Teotihuacán, located about 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Arrange an exclusive early-access tour before the crowds arrive — climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead with your expert archaeologist guide. Optionally, experience a hot air balloon ride over the pyramids at sunrise for a truly unforgettable luxury perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City and explore the upscale Polanco neighborhood — often called the 'Beverly Hills of Mexico City.' Browse flagship boutiques and international luxury brands along Presidente Masaryk Avenue. Visit the world-renowned Museo Soumaya (free entry), home to one of Latin America's finest private art collections including works by Rodin, Dalí, and Monet.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sophisticated dinner at Quintonil in Polanco, helmed by Chef Jorge Vallejo — a celebration of modern Mexican cuisine using hyper-local, seasonal ingredients. Follow dinner with craft cocktails at a nearby speakeasy-style mezcal bar such as Hanky Panky or La Clandestina.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — avocado toast on artisan sourdough, huevos rancheros with salsa verde, fresh-pressed juices, and single-origin pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch box arranged by your private guide at Teotihuacán — local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh tamales, seasonal fruit, and sparkling water; or dine at La Gruta, a dramatic restaurant built inside a natural cave near the pyramids
meals.dinner: Quintonil — contemporary tasting menu with beverage pairing (approx. $120–$200 USD per person; advance reservation required)

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon experience over Teotihuacán must be booked weeks in advance through operators like Globos Aeroestáticos. Depart early (around 7:00 AM) to beat the crowds and heat. Bring sunscreen and a hat for the pyramid climb.

day_by_day.morning: Start the morning with a private Mexican cooking class led by a celebrated local chef — learn to make fresh corn tortillas from scratch, classic mole negro, ceviche, and churros with artisan chocolate dipping sauce. This immersive hands-on experience is held in a beautifully appointed culinary studio in the Roma or Condesa neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the bohemian and architecturally stunning neighborhoods of Colonia Roma and Condesa on a curated walking tour. Admire the Art Deco and Porfirian architecture, visit independent art galleries, and relax in the lush Parque México. Stop at a specialty coffee shop for a single-origin Chiapas or Veracruz pour-over. Browse high-end local design shops and bookstores.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a private Lucha Libre (Mexican wrestling) viewing at Arena México with premium ringside seats — a wildly entertaining and deeply cultural Mexican tradition. Afterward, head to a rooftop bar such as Bar Terraza at Hotel Condesa DF or Departamento for panoramic city views and expertly crafted cocktails using artisanal Mexican spirits.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light breakfast at the resort before heading to the cooking class — fresh fruit, yogurt with granola, and café de olla (traditional spiced Mexican coffee)
meals.lunch: Savor the dishes you prepared during your cooking class as a gourmet sit-down meal with wine pairings — included as part of the culinary experience
meals.dinner: Maximo Bistrot in Colonia Roma — farm-to-table French-Mexican fusion by Chef Eduardo García; known for its impeccable seasonal menu and natural wine list (approx. $80–$140 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lucha Libre events at Arena México typically take place on Fridays and Sundays — confirm the schedule and book VIP ringside seats in advance. The cooking class should be reserved at least one week ahead. Roma and Condesa are very walkable — enjoy the neighborhood at a leisurely pace.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed final morning enjoying the resort's luxury spa — indulge in a traditional Temazcal (pre-Hispanic steam ceremony) or a signature deep-tissue massage using locally sourced volcanic stone and aromatic herbs. Afterward, take a leisurely swim and enjoy a final gourmet breakfast on the terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the prestigious Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec — one of the greatest museums in the world, housing extraordinary Aztec, Maya, and Mesoamerican artifacts including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. Explore the vast Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) — the largest urban park in Latin America — for a peaceful afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Conclude your premium Mexico City journey with a farewell dinner at Sud 777, an acclaimed restaurant in the Pedregal neighborhood offering innovative Mexican haute cuisine in a stunning garden setting. Toast to an unforgettable trip with a flight of aged premium tequilas. Return to the resort for a final night of luxury rest before departure.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — a full spread featuring chilaquiles verdes, freshly baked conchas and croissants, smoked salmon, tropical fruit platters, and a mimosa with Mexican sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the museum café or a nearby café in Polanco — tlayudas, fresh guacamole, and agua de jamaica (hibiscus water)
meals.dinner: Sud 777 — innovative tasting menu with premium tequila and wine pairing in a lush garden setting (approx. $100–$180 USD per person; advance reservation recommended)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Anthropology is closed on Mondays — plan accordingly. Book the Temazcal spa experience the day before to secure your preferred time slot. If departing the following morning, arrange your airport transfer with the concierge the evening before. Allow extra time for luggage and checkout.
